definition: Assigning an action label to a video segment — closely related to action recognition with an emphasis on clip-level classification benchmarks such as Kinetics.
details: Assigning an action label to a video segment — closely related to action recognition with an emphasis on clip-level classification benchmarks such as Kinetics.

explainer.lead: Action classification turns a short video segment into a single action label, such as “running” or “playing guitar.” It gives researchers and engineers a clear clip-level task for comparing video models, including on benchmarks such as Kinetics.

tiers.eli5: Imagine watching a very short video and choosing one phrase that describes what is happening. Action classification teaches a computer to make that choice. Instead of describing every person or object, it gives the whole clip one action label.
tiers.practitioner: A model receives a video segment and predicts one action category for the entire clip. Performance can be compared on clip-level benchmarks such as Kinetics. Predictions depend on the chosen segment boundaries, and a single label may be a poor fit when several actions occur in one clip.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a video segment v and a set of action categories Y, action classification learns a mapping f(v) -> y, where y is the clip-level label in Y. It is closely related to action recognition, with an emphasis on clip-level classification benchmarks such as Kinetics. The formulation does not itself specify when or where within the segment the action occurs.

explainer.example: Given a short clip of a person running, an action classifier considers categories such as “running,” “walking,” and “jumping,” then assigns the single label “running” to the entire segment.

usedIn.name: Kinetics
usedIn.detail: A clip-level classification benchmark used to evaluate predictions of action labels for video segments.

usedIn.name: Action recognition research
usedIn.detail: Action classification provides a focused setting for comparing models that assign labels to whole video clips.

explainer.intuition: The task treats a video segment as one example and asks, “Which action best describes this clip?” The answer is a category for the segment as a whole rather than a description of each frame.
howItWorks: Select a video segment to classify.
Use the visual and temporal information in that segment as model input.
Score the possible action categories for the clip.
Return the selected action label for the whole segment.
explainer.whyItMatters: A single clip-level target creates a well-defined way to train and compare video models. Benchmarks such as Kinetics make those comparisons possible across different approaches.
misconceptions: It does not necessarily identify the exact start and end of an action; the input segment is already being classified.
It is not a separate label for every frame: the standard output is one action label for the whole clip.
It is closely related to action recognition, but emphasizes the clip-level classification setting rather than every possible recognition task.
